reports.race_ordering: The importer now acquires the ID lease before findLocalCopies or loadEntriesFromFile touches local journals. An append completed before acquisition is included in classification and causes a divergent incoming fork when necessary. A live owner prevents acquisition. A writer starting afterwards cannot acquire the reserved ID; ordinary SessionManager conflict handling continues it under another ID rather than appending into the importer's journal. The same exclusive reservation survives placement and backup disposal. This is an implementation ordering argument, not an executed race result.

repairs.F1: Archive artifacts remain a tuple array; anchor-member detection now uses some. Missing legacy members receive explicit empty anchors without overwriting supplied bytes.
repairs.F2: openRelocated performs writable adoption before relocation by default. continueRecent's moved-project route uses it. Staged import explicitly opts out under its existing incoming-ID reservation; raw open remains claim-free.
repairs.F3: Writable admission claims the ID with strict lock-error handling, refreshes and classifies disk provenance under that claim, and retains ownership through writable use. Contention refuses admission, as approved by Main. markSessionMoved uses an exclusive private-storage reservation that refuses same-process holders. close retains its claim until queued persistence settles.
repairs.F4: beginWritableAdoption returns a commit/rollback transaction. A departed source remains owned and unchanged while a newly minted continuation is prepared. Rollback drains and deletes transaction-owned initial/current fork outputs before relinquishing its claim, then restores target state. Lifecycle reports integration through cancellable switch work.
repairs.F5: moveTo rollback now includes final header publication, including rejection after bytes land. Artifact relocation is deferred until that publication succeeds. Rollback reverses the journal path and restores metadata without replacing the current entries array, preserving completed concurrent appends. Import publication retains an additional claim through close and cleanup; backup-restoration failures are surfaced rather than merely logged.
repairs.F6: forkFrom claims its minted ID before copying anchors or first publication, refuses pre-existing output paths, and owns cleanup until returning successfully. Failure cleanup handles landed journals and artifact-only failed publication, then releases the minted claim. File storage deletion no longer skips artifact cleanup when the journal is absent.

race_ordering: Import validates and stages the archive, then exclusively claims its incoming session ID before discovering, reading or classifying local journals.
